_comment: Search terms for the auction scanner. models = high-precision, low-volume, product names. designers = surnames — each with a plain-ASCII/no-hyphen variant too, since sellers on different platforms (Tradera vs Auctionet vs dba.dk) spell the same name differently: 'Carl-Axel Acking' on one, 'Carl Axel Acking' on another, diacritics dropped on a third. lazy_listing_terms = the alpha list, words a seller uses when they don't know what they have. no_designer_items = from research/itens.md section 2, style/wood/type searches without a designer name. woods = valuable/distinctive woods worth searching alone or combined with a seating type. exclude = negative filter, drop any lot whose title matches these. Source: research/itens.md, research/auction-scanner.md section 3, designer research 2026-09-16.

model_designers._comment: Every entry in models[] mapped to its designer, so the dashboard's designer badge always shows even when the listing title doesn't separately repeat the designer's name. Blank/omitted = no single named designer (collective/anonymous series or unclear attribution) — leave it off rather than guess. Source: Sarah, 2026-09-21.

model_database_comment: Rich per-model commercial/sourcing record — vedda_status (BUY/MAYBE/PRESERVE/PASS), upholstery_strategy, price thresholds, multilingual search_terms. Built 2026-09-21 from Sarah's BUY/MAYBE tables plus her explicit collector-sensitive PRESERVE/PASS list. All prices are working sourcing thresholds, not verified market data — see each entry's price_basis field. models[]/model_designers/designers above are kept in sync with this for the existing flat-list scanner (fetch_*.py) — the scanner does NOT yet search the multilingual search_terms objects per model; that requires a separate engine change (see Sarah's session notes 2026-09-21). PK61 (a table) is deliberately excluded from models[]/model_designers/designers — kept here for reference only, seating_only would drop it anyway.
